Butters is a Bulldog

Zak Butters is officially a Western Bulldog. Port Adelaide will not match the offer and accept pick No. 5 as compensation, having also earlier secured picks 6, 10, and two future-firsts in the five-club mega trade. The star free agent and three-time All-Australian, who played 156 games and kicked 73 goals for the Power after being drafted in 2019, has signed a nine-year deal with his boyhood club

Hawks land spearhead King

After securing Zach Merrett earlier this week, Hawthorn have officially welcomed Ben King today after gold Coast elected not to match the offer for the restricted free agent. the Suns will receive a first round pick as compensation, which currently stands at pick No. 7.

Mega trade approved

The league approved a mega trade involving Port Adelaide, the Bulldogs, Melbourne, Hawthorn and Carlton, two players and scores of picks.

Under the five-team deal, the Bulldogs gave up picks No. 12 and No. 31 and a 2028 first-rounder to bring in Hawthorn's Finn Maginness, Carlton's Hudson O'Keeffe and later picks in this year's draft and future years.

Port parted with picks No. 4, 46 and 81 and six second-round or worse future selections to get back picks No. 6 and No. 10, Melbourne's 2027 first-rounder and the Dogs' 2028 first-rounder.

The Demons surrendered picks No.6, 10 and 87 and their 2027 first-rounder -- as well as two late future picks -- for picks No. 4, 12, 31 and 46.

Hawthorn (2027 third-rounder) and Carlton (2028 fourth-rounder) received late future picks for Maginness and O'Keeffe.

-- AAP

Flag Lion gets his wish

Brisbane has traded second-year Lion and 2025 premiership player Sam Marshall and pick No. 39 to St Kilda for a 2027 first-rounder.

Thursday, Oct. 8
Marshall lands at the Cats

St Kilda have pulled the trigger on a deal to send contracted ruckman Rowan Marshall to Geelong, as the Cats and other rival clubs circle Sydney star Nick Blakey.

Geelong traded pick No.14 in this year's draft for the disenchanted 30-year-old and a third-round selection in 2028 on Thursday afternoon.

New Zealand-born Marshall had requested a move to the Cats for a second straight year after St Kilda recruited Tom De Koning to become their first-choice ruckman.

-- AAP

Wednesday, Oct. 7
Dons defender gets traded to the Cats

After being denied a trade last year, Jordan Ridley got his wish for a fresh start after Essendon and Geelong agreed to a deal on Wednesday.

Geelong gave up utility Jack Bowes, a 2027 first-round pick and 2028 second-round pick to get the 27-year-old Ridley through the door.

Pick No. 60 and a 2028 fourth-round selection will come back to the Cats from the Bombers.

--AAP

Tuesday, Oct. 6
O'Driscoll makes the move over east

Fremantle have traded 24-year-old Nathan O'Driscoll to Richmond in exchange for pick 61 in this year's draft.

The winger played 17 games for the Dockers this season but wasn't selected for the Grand Final.

Monday, Oct. 5
TRADE PERIOD OPENS
Merrett finally becomes a Hawk

After attempting to join Hawthorn last year, Zach Merrett has finally been traded from Essendon to the Hawks.

Hawthorn have sent picks 15, 25 and a 2028 second-round pick in exchange for the 31-year-old.

Merrett leaves the Bombers a week after winning a record-equaling seventh Crichton Medal, three All-Australian blazers, and 274 games.

Pendlebury becomes a Sun

AFL games record holder Scott Pendlebury is officially a Sun after Gold Coast and Collingwood agreed on a trade for the 38-year-old veteran.

Pendlebury, a two-time premiership player, heads to the Suns in exchange for pick No. 65 in this year's draft.

"It's an exciting group here at the SUNS and the opportunity to bring a few different ideas and also learn from a great group of coaches and players is one I'm really looking forward to," Pendlebury told the Suns.

"This side is one I've watched from afar and really admired. I've got a bit of knowledge about the industry so I'm here to play my role and help this squad continue to develop."

Jesse Hogan traded from GWS to Collingwood

Out-of-favour Giants forward Jesse Hogan has made the switch to Collingwood in exchange for pick 75.

The 31-year-old won the Coleman Medal in 2024 but has been unable to recapture his best form at the Giants in the two years since.

Magpies list boss Justin Leppitsch said Hogan would be a valuable addition.

"On behalf of everyone at Collingwood, I'd like to warmly welcome Jesse to Collingwood. Jesse has established himself as one of the competition's premier key forwards and we're excited to see him bring his experience and talent to our club," he said.

"His aerial presence inside forward-50 and his consistency as a goal-kicker make him a genuine threat.

"Like Lachie (Neale), Jesse has a passion to teach the next generation and will make a great addition to our club."

Saturday, Oct. 3
Bulldogs seal free-agency signing of key defender

The Western Bulldogs have finally snagged the key defender they need, securing Adelaide backman Jordon Butts as an unrestricted free agent.

The Bulldogs are set for a bumper AFL trade period headlined by working through a deal for Port Adelaide superstar Zak Butters, ahead of a 2027 season where the club will have high expectations.

But after seeing off Carlton's advances to keep hold of defender Buku Khamis, the Bulldogs have filled a major area of need by adding 26-year-old Butts.

Adelaide will receive a second-round compensation selection, currently pick No.33, in this year's draft.

-- AAP

Friday, Oct. 2
FREE AGENCY OPEN
Three-peat Lion locks in Magpies move

Lachie Neale has sealed his high-profile switch to Collingwood, with Brisbane teasing the dual Brownlow medallist on his way out the door.

The AFL approved Neale signing a three-year deal with the Magpies on Friday afternoon, closing out the first day of free agency.

The 33-year-old ball-winner leaves as an unrestricted free agent after the Lions clinched a third straight flag with their stunning seven-point grand final victory over Fremantle.

-- AAP

Greene on his way to the Cats

Toby Greene will join Geelong as an unrestricted free agent on a three-year deal, re-partnering with former Giants teammate Jeremey Cameron.

The paperwork was lodged to the AFL on Friday morning.

The Giants receive band three compensation for Greene, which is currently pick No. 26 in the upcoming draft.

Greene departs the Giants with his name etched in the club's record books, sitting first in games played for the club with a tally of 282 games, as well as leading the club's all-time goalkicking tally with 450 majors.

Briggs now a Tiger

Richmond has landed GWS ruck Kieren Briggs as an unrestricted free agent.

Briggs' move to the Tigers was confirmed just hours after the free agency window opened on Friday.

Briggs played 88 games for GWS after joining the club as the No.34 pick in the 2018 draft.

Amartey officially joins the Blues

Free agency has opened with a bang, with out-of-favour key forward Joel Amartey committing to Carlton.

Details are still to come on the length of contract, and Sydney's compensation.

Hawthorn father-son recommits despite interest

Calsher Dear has made a shock decision to re-sign with the Hawks for two years, despite being out of favour thorughout 2026.

The 20-year-old has kicked 39 goals from 31 games, but found himself behind Jack Gunston, Mitch Lewis and Mabior Chol. With Gunston signed on and Suns forward Ben King expected to sign with the Hawks as well, there were questions about whether Dear would get enough opportunity at his childhood club.

Hawks list boss Mark McKenzie said the club was "really pleased" that Dear had recommitted.

"He remains an important part of what we are trying to achieve as a club," he said.

"Following his debut season, Calsher showed us all the special talent that he is, but as a key tall at 21 years of age, we've needed to be patient with his progression.

"Having battled several injuries over his first three seasons in the system, we are very excited about what the future holds for Calsher with a strong pre-season under his belt and greater continuity into 2027 and beyond."

Thursday, Oct. 1
Goater set to make cross-city switch

North Melbourne defender Josh Goater is set to join the Hawks after requesting a trade on Thursday.

Having played just 18 games, the 23-year-old had fallen out of favour after an injury-hit run in his time at North.

Premiership Lion requests trade

The Brisbane Lions have confirmed Sam Marshall has requested a trade to St Kilda.

"The Brisbane Lions confirm premiership midfielder Sam Marshall has requested to be traded to St Kilda," the Lions said in a statement.

"Marshall has played 13 games, including the 2025 Premiership, across two seasons since being selected in the first round of the 2024 draft as a graduate of the Youi Brisbane Lions Academy.

"The club respects Marshall's request to be traded, and will work towards facilitating an outcome that best reflects true value to the Brisbane Lions for the 20-year-old."

Tuesday, Sept. 29
Neale informs Lions he intends to join Collingwood

Two-time Brownlow Medal winner Lachie Neale has told Brisbane he will depart the club as an unrestricted free agent and sign a three-year deal with Collingwood.

Aware that Neale intended to leave at the end of the year, the Lions never offered him a new contract.

The paperwork for the deal is expected to be formalised as early as Friday when the free agency period opens.

Friday, Sept. 25
Jordon Butts to join the Bulldogs

Zak Butters isn't the only South Australian-based player keen to join the Western Bulldogs, with Crows' key defender Jordon Butts officially naming the Dogs as his preferred offseason destination.

The unrestricted free agent will sign a five-year deal at the Kennel, according to AFL.com.au.

Tuesday, Sept. 22
Amartey officially names Carlton

Wantaway Sydney forward Joel Amartey has confirmed his desire to join Carlton as an unrestricted free agent.

The 26-year-old was kept out of the Swans' side with an Achilles injury in the latter stages of the year.

With Charlie Curnow (75 goals in 2026) and Logan McDonald (51) cementing their spots in the Sydney forward line as the prime targets, Amartey is hoping for more opportunity at the Blues.

Thursday, Sept. 17
GWS captain finally makes big call on his future

Toby Greene has opted to leave GWS, telling the AFL club he wishes to play with Geelong next season. Greene, who has been at the Giants since their foundation season in 2012, wants to go back to Victoria for family reasons.

In an extraordinary way to announce the decision, outgoing GWS boss Dave Matthews confirmed Greene's intentions on radio, before the club released a statement.

The 32-year-old has been offered a lucrative three-year deal to join the Cats.

Saturday, Sept. 12
Zak Butters makes huge free agency call
The year's hottest restricted free agent Zak Butters has made a huge call on his future, nominating the Western Bulldogs as his preferred destination.

After a year of speculation, with Geelong thought to be the front-runner for the Power star's signature, Butters made the call on Saturday, first reported by AFL.com.au's Callum Twomey.

The deal is reportedly for nine years.

Thursday, Sept. 10
Hogan set to join Pies
GWS and Collingwood have both confirmed that 2024 Coleman Medal winner Jesse Hogan has chosen the Magpies at his next home.

Set to be a four-club player, Hogan is 31 and coming off a 12-goal season from just nine appearances.

It's a big boost for the Magpies if Hogan can recapture his form; key forward has been an area of concern for a number of years.

Tuesday, Sept. 8
Bailey set to be Lion for life
Brisbane's Zac Bailey has ended months of 'will he, won't he' speculation to sign with the Lions for eight years, taking him through the 2034 season, the the club confirmed on Tuesday.

Bailey, a free agent, had been a big target for the Crows, who had reportedly tabled a more lucrative offer.

"I'm absolutely rapt to be staying at the Brisbane Lions," Bailey said in a statement.

"I love the environment here, the players, coaches and staff who all make it a great place to be and I feel like this Club continues to bring the best out of me.

"This Club means so much to me - I came here as a young player and have grown up here and to know I will be here long-term is something I'm really proud of.

"I would like to thank the club, my partner Em, my family and my management for being so supportive throughout this process.

"I love what we as a club have achieved during my time here and I am super excited about what we can continue to achieve together."

Rowan Marshall requests trade
St Kilda ruck Rowan Marshall looks set to be on the move, with the Saints confirming the big man had requested a trade for the second straight season.

While Marshall hasn't requested a specific club, it's likely to be Geelong after he failed to secure a trade to the Cats last year. He played 21 games for the Saints this seaosn, juggling ruck duties with Tom De Koning, who came in from Carlton last offseason.

"Rowan is a highly valued member of the St Kilda Football Club and remains contracted until the end of 2027," the Saints said in a statement.

"Marshall has not nominated a preferred destination at this stage, with the club making clear that any trade will need to be in the best interests of the St Kilda Football Club."

Zane Duursma wants to go to Melbourne
The No. 4 pick in the 2023 AFL draft Zane Duursma has requested a trade out of North Melbourne, with Melbourne in his sights.

The news comes a week after coach Alastair Clarkson was sacked by the club. North won nine games in 2026, their best return since 2019.

Ed Allan re-signs with the Pies
After speculation about his future at the Magpies, mdifielder Ed Allan has put pen to paper, signing a four year extension to remain at Collingwood.

2026 was a breakout season for Allan, who played 19 games and averaged a career-high 16.5 disposals per game.

Monday, Sept. 7
Pair of in-demand Dogs re-sign
According to afl.com.au, both Arty Jones and Buku Khamis will remain at the Kennel this offseason.

Jones will sign a three-year deal, while Khamis has a five-year contract in front of him.

Essendon and Brisbane had interest in livewire forward Jones, who had a standout performance against Collingwood in the wildcard final win, while the Blues were heavily linked to Khamis for a second straight offseason.

Cooper Hodge nomintes Hawthorn
A big boost for the Hawks, with club champion Luke Hodge's son Cooper choosing to join the Melbourne-based team as a father-son at this year's draft.

He had the option of going to Brisbane as a Lions academy member.

stories.headline: Messi tracker: Goals, assists, key moments in 2026
stories.summary: ESPN provides game-by-game analysis of Lionel Messi's performances for Inter Miami and Argentina.
stories.body:
Lionel Messi will aim for more success in 2026. His Inter Miami side captured its first MLS Cup title last season and will look to defend it -- and add further silverware too -- in its first season at Nu Stadium, the club's new home.

Messi also captained Argentina as they fell just one step short of defending their FIFA World Cup crown, losing 1-0 in extra time to Spain in the final of what could be his last tournament.

As the 39-year-old continues to feature for both club and country, ESPN will track his performances game-by-game, providing stats and analysis each time he pulls on a Herons or Albiceleste jersey.

Messi's 2026 tally:

Games played: 41
Goals: 38
Assists: 17

Oct. 10: Inter Miami 4-0 D.C. United

Back in the pink of Inter Miami, and back in the goals for Messi.

His two strikes sealed an emphatic 4-0 win for the Herons over D.C. United at Nu Stadium on Saturday night.

After Luis Suárez had Miami 2-0 up after 39 minutes Messi scored his first in the 47th, retrieving a pass from the Uruguayan before tapping in a shot inside the right post.

Messi then padded the hosts' lead in the 60th minute, latching on to Rodrigo De Paul's pass, before dribbling inside the area, eluding two United defenders and firing past goalkeeper Sean Johnson with a shot from 12 yards.

Oct. 6: Argentina 3-0 Benin

It was an emotionally charged night in Buenos Aires as Messi played his final international match for Argentina, the team that he had led to World Cup glory and two Copa América titles as captain.

The friendly match at the Estadio Monumental was goalless at halftime, but just a few minutes after the break Messi's in-swinging corner from the left was rattled home on the volley by Nicolás Otamendi.

Then, on the hour mark, Messi spotted Nico Paz in space 25 yards from goal. He fed a square pass with the outside of his boot to the Como player, who curled in a classy finish.

But the night undoubtedly belonged to Messi, and he fired a penalty into the top corner to cap off his 208th and final senior appearance for his country with his 126th goal.

Sep. 27: Columbus Crew 2-1 Inter Miami
Before heading to Argentina for his final international match, Messi gave Miami fans something to savor in Ohio.

From a set piece wide on the right wing and with most of those in the stadium, including those in the Columbus defense, surely expecting a cross, Messi's left foot sent the ball curling wickedly into the far top corner of the net.

Messi had chances to add to that tally in the second half but was denied from distance by Columbus goalkeeper Patrick Schulte and put another effort into the side netting.

Then Jamal Thiaré scored in the eighth minute of second-half stoppage time to give the Columbus Crew a stunning 2-1 win.

Sep. 20: Inter Miami 2-2 San Diego FC

Messi's sublime curling free kick was not enough to inspire the Herons to a win against San Diego on Sunday night.

After falling behind to an Anders Dreyer goal in the 12th minute, 39-year-old Messi levelled the scores with beautiful set-piece shot in the 24th minute. His well-hit effort evaded a number of attackers and defenders before sneaking in at the far post.

Miami thought they'd won the match after Luiz Suarez fired the hosts ahead in the 74th minute, only for Dreyer to nab his second goal of the game and ensure the points were shared.

Sep. 16: Inter Miami 2-0 Cruz Azul

Another day, another trophy for Messi.

The Argentine master scored his 100th goal for Inter Miami as the Herons defeated Cruz Azul 2-0 on Wednesday night to win the Campeones Cup.

Messi opened the scoring in the 24th minute, heading in a cross from Luis Suárez, before turning provider for Casemiro -- sending in a corner for the Brazilian to nod home.

Sep. 12: Inter Miami 2-2 Nashville SC
In a matchup between the two best teams in the Eastern Conference, the action went end to end, with Messi getting on the scoresheet for Miami's second goal off a Rodrigo De Paul assist as he continues to lead the Golden Boot race.

Ultimately, the teams settled for a point apiece, as the hosts failed to close the gap on Nashville at the top of the table.

Sep. 9: Chicago Fire 1-1 Inter Miami

Two or Europe's greatest club players took center stage in one of the United States' most iconic American football stadiums on Wednesday -- and a record crowd came out to watch.

Ex-Bayern Munich and Barcelona star Robert Lewandowski scored a trademark acrobatic goal in the 10th minute to give the Fire an early lead at the NFL home of the Chicago Bears.

But Inter Miami drew level shortly after halftime when Casemiro, another of the game's stars with a long history of playing in Europe before moving to MLS, headed home a Messi cross from a corner kick to make it 1-1.

The assist was Messi's league-leading 13th of the season. He also has league 18 goals and is the first player in MLS history with 30-plus goal contributions in three separate seasons.

Sep. 5: Inter Miami 2-2 Atlanta United
Messi was not as effective as he was in the previous matchup, but he did get an assist for Casemiro's opening goal. However, his team was unable to win as they had to settle for a point in a 2-2 draw.

August 29: Inter Miami 7-1 CF Montréal

Fans were treated to a Messi masterclass on Saturday as the Argentine magician registered four goals and an assist to help Miami to a club-record 7-1 victory over CF Montréal.

Messi scored with a deflected free kick in the 40th minute before netting after a stunning solo run in the 52nd. After supplying an assist to Luis Suárez, the 39-year-old then completed his hat trick and with a delicate chip over the goalkeeper with seven minutes of regulation time remaining.

He wasn't done yet.

Deep into stoppage time, Messi lined up a free kick and dispatched it with trademark precision into the top corner of the net. Legendary stuff.

August 22: Inter Miami 2-1 Toronto FC

Messi's 14th MLS goal of the season wasn't enough to prevent Inter Miami from slumping to their fourth loss in their last five games, losing 2-1 to Toronto FC at Nu Stadium on Saturday.

Messi found the net with a first-time finish from a Rodrigo De Paul through-ball with eight minutes remaining, but the home side's late rally fell short of salvaging a much-needed draw to bolster the Herons' pursuit of first-placed Nashville SC in the Eastern Conference.

August 19: Inter Miami 2-2 Philadelphia Union

Messi is back scoring goals, but unfortunately, his Miami side is not back to winning ways. The Argentine scored Miami's second goal of the night as both teams finished with 10 men. Miami are now winless in their last four matches.

August 15: Nashville SC 4-1 Inter Miami
It was not the best night for Messi in Tennessee. The Argentine missed yet another penalty -- his third straight for club and country -- and they suffered a heavy 4-1 loss to their Eastern Conference rivals. However, he did get an assist for Telasco Segovia's equalizer at halftime before Miami lost control in the second half.

August 12: Inter Miami 2-3 Club León
Just days after the passing of his father, Messi came off the bench in the second half to try to help Miami continue in the Leagues Cup after they were leading 1-0. However, it ended in a 3-2 loss which saw them eliminated in the league phase after a second straight loss, coming off defeat to Monterrey last weekend with Messi away at the memorial for his father.

August 5: Inter Miami 4-2 Atlético de San Luis

Lionel Messi made his first start for Inter Miami since returning from the World Cup and picked up right where he left off, scoring a stellar pair of goals to guide his team to a come-from-behind 4-2 rout of Atlético de San Luis in its first game of the 2026 Leagues Cup.

Messi's first goal was an exquisite volley, redirecting Noah Allen's cross from the left flank while running at full speed. Miami's third goal of the opening half -- and Messi's second on the night -- came on the back of some intricate buildup play with Allen once again setting up his team captain, this time in the center of the area where he tiptoed through two defenders and buried a close-range strike past Andrés Sánchez.

The goal made Messi the all-time leading scorer in Leagues Cup history with 14, one ahead of LAFC's Denis Bouanga since the expanded competition began in 2023.

August 1: Inter Miami 2-2 Columbus Crew
Messi made his return to action for Inter Miami on Saturday, 13 days after tasting defeat with Argentina in the World Cup final. The Miami talisman started on the substitutes' bench before being introduced in the 53rd minute of the Herons' 2-2 draw with the Columbus Crew at Nu Stadium in Miami.

July 19: Spain 1-0 AET Argentina

Sunday proved to be a bridge too far for both Messi and Argentina, falling in extra time to Spain in the World Cup final.

With La Roja controlling the match basically from start to finish -- Argentina didn't register a shot on target during regulation time -- Messi had few opportunities to impact the game. Indeed, the 39-year-old was given a 3/10 in ESPN's post-match player ratings.

Still, as Mark Ogden points out, the 2026 tournament was a memorable one for Messi and cemented his status as the GOAT, if it were ever in doubt.

July 15: England 1-2 Argentina
Messi made another statement in his 205th appearance for Argentina, this time in his first-ever match against England in a World Cup semifinal. With so much at stake for both nations, Messi once again proved decisive despite not getting on the scoresheet.

He first provided the assist for Enzo Fernández's superb strike to level the match in the second half before delivering a pinpoint cross for Lautaro Martínez's headed winner, sending the reigning champions into yet another World Cup final after another dramatic encounter.

Messi has now recorded either a goal or an assist in all seven of Argentina's matches at this World Cup, and he will have the opportunity to lift the trophy for a second time when Argentina face Spain in Sunday's final in New Jersey.

July 11: Argentina 3-1 Switzerland
It was a relatively quiet night by Messi's standards as his goalscoring streak came to an end, but his influence on the match stayed the same. He set up Alexis Mac Allister's opening goal for Argentina against Switzerland, and although the match went to extra time, the defending champions won 3-1 thanks to two late goals in the second half of extra time.

Messi's quest to retain the World Cup now continues into the semifinals, where Argentina will face England for the first time in over 20 years. The clash in Atlanta -- one of international soccer's most storied rivalries -- will decide a spot in the final.

July 7: Argentina 3-2 Egypt
It was another dramatic outing for Messi and Argentina, who rallied from a 2-0 deficit to defeat Egypt 3-2 in Atlanta and book their place in the World Cup quarterfinals. As is so often the case, Messi was at the center of the action. Minutes after Egypt opened the scoring, he missed another penalty, but he quickly made amends by setting up Cristian Romero for Argentina's first goal. Messi then scored the equalizer -- his eighth goal of the tournament -- before Enzo Fernández completed the comeback with the winner. Argentina will now face Switzerland in Kansas City for a place in the semifinals.

July 3: Argentina 3-2 Cape Verde
Messi suffered a major scare in Miami Gardens on Friday evening in the round of 32, but it ultimately ended well for Argentina. He opened the scoring with his seventh goal of the tournament, extending his World Cup tally to 20 goals while finding the net in a record eighth consecutive World Cup match. Cape Verde twice fought back -- once in the second half and again in extra time -- but the world champions eventually prevailed 3-2 after extra time to book a meeting in the round of 16 with Egypt.

June 27: Jordan 1-3 Argentina
Messi didn't play the full 90 minutes in Argentina's 3-1 win over an already-eliminated Jordan, but he still made his mark during a 30-minute cameo in Texas. The 39-year-old scored a free kick for his sixth goal of the tournament and his 19th career World Cup goal, becoming the first player ever to score in seven consecutive World Cup matches. Even at 39, he's still got it.

June 22: Argentina 2-0 Austria
Another chapter in an already unparalleled career. Lionel Messi scored twice in Argentina's 2-0 win over Austria to help his team qualify for the round of 32 and become the outright leading goalscorer in men's and women's FIFA World Cup history with 18 goals. After missing an early penalty, he responded by breaking Miroslav Klose's 12-year-old record and then added a second late on to break Marta's record. All just two days before turning 39.

June 16: Argentina 3-0 Algeria
In his 200th appearance for Argentina and sixth World Cup, Lionel Messi sent a message to the world just days before his 39th birthday: he still has it. His first-ever World Cup hat trick powered Argentina to victory in their group-stage opener, while his 16th tournament goal saw him draw level with Miroslav Klose for the most goals in World Cup history.

June 9: Argentina 3-0 Iceland

Messi, working his way back from muscle fatigue ahead of the start of the World Cup, came on in the 70th minute of a pre-tournament friendly in Auburn, Alabama and scored from the penalty spot right afterward.

It was Messi's 911th career goal for club and country and 117th goal for Argentina and made him the oldest scorer in the country's soccer history.

May 24: Inter Miami 6-4 Philadelphia Union

Messi registered two assists in a scintillating performance against Philadelphia on Sunday but, unfortunately, no one was focused on results come the end of the game.

That's because, in the very last game before the World Cup, Messi left the field in the 73rd minute and headed straight to the locker room after grabbing his left thigh.

Now, supporters around the world are holding their collective breath while they wait and see if the injury has scuppered the 38-year-old's chance of appearing at a sixth World Cup.

May 13: FC Cincinnati 3-5 Inter Miami

Two goals and one assist marked yet another spectacular contribution from Miami superstar Messi on Wednesday. The Argentine magician was instrumental as the Herons fought back from 3-2 down to eventually beat Cincinnati 5-3 at TQL Stadium in Ohio.

May 9: Toronto FC 2-4 Inter Miami

It was a day of star power. Not only were Rodrigo De Paul, Luis Suárez and Sergio Reguilón all on the score sheet for the Herons, so was Messi -- and he added a pair of assists, too.

While Miami has yet to taste victory at its new home, it continues to take care of business on the road. Saturday's win in Toronto extended the club's unbeaten record away from home in 2026 to seven games, picking up six wins and one draw in the first few months of the season.

May 2: Inter Miami 3-4 Orlando City

Messi notched a goal and an assist on Saturday in what ended up being an astonishing collapse for Inter Miami at Nu Stadium.

The Herons were leading 3-0 after Messi's classy 33rd-minute strike, but gifted the visitors four goals -- including a Martín Ojeda hat trick -- to once again miss out on a victory at their new home ground. Orlando's comeback from three goals down marks only the third time in MLS history that a team has claimed all three points after trailing by three or more goals.

As for Messi's Miami, only twice has an MLS team had a longer winless run -- now up to four for the Herons -- to open up a new stadium.

April 25: Inter Miami 1-1 New England Revolution
Messi again failed to get on the scoresheet as Miami put in a fatigued second-half performance that saw them come from a goal down against New England. It was another draw -- and another game without a win at their new home, Nu Stadium.

April 22: Real Salt Lake 0-2 Inter Miami
No goals or assists from Messi as Miami visited America First Field on Wednesday, but the fans did get treated to sumptuous strikes nonetheless.

Rodrigo De Paul's opener in the 80th-minute was stunning curler from outside the box and then, almost immediately after the restart, Luis Suarez made it 2-0 with a well-struck volley.

The victory moves Inter Miami into outright second in the MLS Eastern Conference.

April 18: Colorado Rapids 2-3 Inter Miami

Another moment of Messi magic bagged all three points for Inter Miami on Saturday.

With scores level in the 79th minute, the Argentine icon danced his way past a number of Colorado defenders before curling home an outrageous effort into the far corner.

The strike -- Messi's second of the match after converting a penalty in the first half -- helped Miami to their first win under interim coach Guillermo Hoyos.

Hoyos, who had been serving as club's sporting director, took over coaching duties after Javier Mascherano unexpectedly left the club due to personal reasons last week.

April 11: Inter Miami 2-2 Red Bull New York
Miami and Messi are still waiting for a first win at Nu Stadium after a 2-2 draw with Red Bull New York on Saturday night.

Messi didn't register a goal or assist, but did help set up Germán Berterame's second-half strike that gave Inter Miami its first lead at its new home ground, but 17-year-old Adri Mehmeti's first career goal in the 77th minute secured a point for the visitors.

April 4: Inter Miami 2-2 Austin FC
Inter Miami opened Nu Stadium the only way it knows how: With a Messi goal. The No. 10 began the move in trademark style with a left-footed pass to a teammate before moving past a defender and arriving in the box at just the right time to head past goalkeeper Brad Stuver.

March 31: Argentina 5-0 Zambia
It was the last day of the month and perhaps the last game for Messi playing for Argentina playing in his native country, but they put on a show defeating the African side Zambia 5-0. Messi scored the second goal for Lionel Scaloni's side as focus will shift now to Miami until the beginning of the World Cup.

March 27: Argentina 2-1 Mauritania
In his first game for his country in 2026, Messi only played the second half as Argentina won 2-1 against Mauritania at the mythical La Bombonera in Buenos Aires, as the World Cup champions continue to prepare to defend their title this summer in North America.

March 22: NYCFC 2-3 Inter Miami

It was a thrilling encounter in the Bronx, as the Argentine star helped his team to a 3-2 win over NYCFC, which also included another trademark free kick goal, now beginning his course for potentially 1,000 career goals. Only 99 goals left!

March 18: Inter Miami 1-1 Nashville SC

Messi may have made history on Wednesday night, becoming just the second men's player in history to score 900 career goals, but it wasn't enough to seal Miami's progress in the Concacaf Champions Cup.

The Argentina legend found the back of the net in the seventh minute at Chase Stadium, but his strike was cancelled out by Nashville's Cristian Espinoza -- sealing the Herons' tournament exit on the away goals rule.

March 11: Nashville SC 0-0 Inter Miami
A drab night for Messi and Co. in the Concacaf Champions Cup. Plenty of possession but few shots on target mean that the Herons will return to Chase Stadium know a win will be needed to ensure progression.

March 7: D.C. United 1-2 Inter Miami

It was quite an eventful week for Messi. Just days before Miami's match against D.C. United, Messi and the entire squad visited the White House and met President Donald Trump and were eager to put on a show for the sold-out crowd of over 70,000 at Baltimore's M&T Bank Stadium.

And they did just that, with a 2-1 win over D.C. United. Messi, of course, scored Miami's second and is now one goal away from 900 career goals.

March 1: Orlando City 2-4 Inter Miami

Well, that blip didn't last long! Messi and Miami roared back into life with a 4-2 thrashing of Orlando on Sunday thanks to the 38-year-old's wizardry.

Things looked ominous for the Herons after the first 45 minutes, down 2-0 and looking on course to start the MLS season with two bleak losses.

But two goals and an assist from Messi in the second half dragged the visitors back in the game and helped secure Miami their first points of the season.

Feb. 21: LAFC 3-0 Inter Miami
Messi and Miami aimed to start 2026 firing on all cylinders, but it was the hosts who spoiled the defending MLS Cup champions' opener at the LA Coliseum. In front of a sellout crowd of 75,673 -- the second-highest attendance in MLS history -- Miami were outplayed, with LAFC's Denis Bouanga getting a goal and an assist in a convincing home victory.

The main talking point, however, emerged after the final whistle. Messi was initially reported to have gained unauthorized access to the officials' locker room after video circulated showing him near the area. However, it was later reported that no league policy had been violated and Messi was cleared of any wrongdoing. Miami will now turn its attention next weekend against fellow Florida side Orlando City.

stories.headline: NRL: Spencer Leniu signs with Eels after early Roosters release
stories.summary: Spencer Leniu has signed a four-year deal with Parramatta just days after winning his fourth NRL premiership with the Sydney Roosters.
stories.body:
Spencer Leniu has signed a four-year deal with Parramatta just days after winning his fourth NRL premiership with the Sydney Roosters.

Leniu finished his three-year stint at the Tricolours on a high after a stellar performance in their 19-18 win over Newcastle to secure the 2026 trophy.

The NSW Origin representative added the Roosters' premiership ring to the three he won with Penrith from 2021-2023.

Leniu was granted a release from the final year of his Roosters contract, which will give the club some salary cap reprieve

The hard-hitting forward's Eels contract is reportedly worth more than the $850,000 per year he was making with Easts, where he spent much of his time coming off the bench.

He is expected to play a more active role in blue and gold, leading the line for the Eels' forward pack.

The westward move will see the former Panther reunite with good friend Jarome Luai, but first the pair will both suit up for Toa Samoa at the Rugby League World Cup.

Eels general manager of football Mark O'Neill shared his delight at signing one of the game's "premier enforcers".

"We're thrilled to have Spencer join the Parramatta Eels and become part of what we're building at this club," O'Neill said in a statement.

"He's one of the elite middle forwards in the game and has consistently performed on the biggest stages throughout his career.

The exit of Leniu adds to the exodus of stars from the Roosters premiership lineup.

Angus Crichton and Mark Nawaqanitawase are rugby-bound, Daly Cherry-Evans is joining Hull FC, while Daniel Tupou retired this week after his 307-game career.

Connor Watson, who missed the title decider due to concussion, has signed for a season with St George Illawarra Dragons.

Roosters coach Trent Robinson said Leniu had been a strong contributor during his time at the club.

"Spencer has brought a lot to our group over the last three years, both through the way he plays and the energy and personality he brings every day," Robinson said in a statement on Thursday.

"He brings an intensity and competitiveness to everything he does, and he challenges the people around him to be better.

"To see him finish his time here as a premiership winner is something he should be really proud of, and something we'll always share together."

With his departure announced at the Roosters' awards night on Wednesday, Leniu said he would leave the club on a high.

""I'm proud to have worn the Roosters jersey and I'll always have a lot of love and respect for the club, the boys and everyone who has supported me during my time here," said Leniu.

"Winning a premiership with this group and sharing that with the boys, our families and everyone at the club is something I'll carry with me for the rest of my life."

stories.headline: Ten arrests, police officer injured, after Liverpool vs. Man City
stories.summary: Merseyside Police have confirmed that 10 people were arrested and an officer sustained a serious injury during the policing operation for Manchester City's clash at Liverpool.
stories.body:
Merseyside Police have confirmed that 10 people were arrested and an officer sustained a serious injury during the policing operation for Manchester City's clash at Liverpool.

Sunday's game at Anfield was the first since City's guilty verdict of financial breaches which they have subsequently appealed, and they were greeted to a febrile atmosphere on Merseyside.

There were hundreds of fans outside Anfield ahead of kickoff, and the City team bus arrived from a back entrance to avoid them. Inside the stadium, the players were greeted by numerous banners, angry chants and jeering.

However, the rancor wasn't restricted to just inside Anfield.

"The arrests included one man arrested on suspicion of two offences of assaulting a constable, five on suspicion of tragedy chanting, one on suspicion of being drunk and disorderly and assault, two for affray and one on suspicion of throwing items onto the pitch," Merseyside Police said in a statement.

"At around 6.35pm, as fans left the stadium, a police officer sustained a serious facial injury during the arrest of a man on Anfield Road. The officer was taken to hospital for treatment and is now recovering at home."

"Football fans who chant about tragedies cause huge distress to the loved ones of people who died and their behaviour has absolutely no place in football," chief inspector Leanne Hobin said.

- The Premier League's new villains: Anfield gives Man City a taste of what's to come

- Man City show defiance in wake of cheating scandal, trounce depleted Liverpool

"We will continue to work with clubs to take action to identify any perpetrators and bring them to justice.

"I hope the arrests today send a clear message and act as a deterrent to others. Anyone who engages in this abhorrent behaviour risks ending up in custody and getting a criminal record."

stories.headline: Source: Steelers' Roman Wilson expected to miss multiple weeks
stories.summary: Roman Wilson will miss multiple weeks because of a finger injury, a source told ESPN, joining the growing list of injured Steelers receivers.
stories.body:
Roman Wilson will miss multiple weeks because of a finger injury, a source told ESPN's Jeremy Fowler, joining the growing list of injured Pittsburgh Steelers wide receivers.

Wilson suffered the injury in the second quarter of Sunday's victory over the Indianapolis Colts. He was seen grabbing his left hand after an incomplete pass attempt from Aaron Rodgers and eventually was ruled out for the rest of the game.

Wilson is still getting more information on the injury and will seek a second opinion, the source told Fowler.

Pittsburgh already is without veteran receiver Michael Pittman Jr., who was placed on injured reserve Saturday because of a foot injury. The Steelers also lost wideout/special teams ace Ben Skowronek, who left in the second quarter Sunday with a calf injury.

With Wilson, Pittman and possibly Skowronek sidelined, the Steelers currently are left with DK Metcalf, rookies Germie Bernard and Kaden Wetjen, and Brandon Smith -- who was elevated from the practice squad Saturday -- as their only healthy receivers.

Wilson, 25, was off to a solid start in his third season with the Steelers. He has 14 receptions on 25 targets for 188 yards and two touchdowns, and entered Sunday's game with the second-most receiving targets on the team.

stories.headline: MLB playoffs: How Rays, Guardians, Brewers, Dodgers were built
stories.summary: How homegrown is each team? What were their signature moves? We break down each club's roster blueprints.
stories.body:
Every contender is built a little differently. That's certainly the case for this year's MLB final four.

We have baseball's biggest revenue team and three clubs that have won with youth and/or efficient spending. We have four franchises with entirely different historical contexts. There are many paths to winning in baseball; here are the ones taken by the last four teams standing in the 2026 season.

How the Milwaukee Brewers were built

Roster style: Young and athletic.

On the heels of a period during which the Brewers featured a power-based lineup full of strikeout-prone sluggers -- remember the "jumbo infield" of the last decade? -- Milwaukee began to put more emphasis on athleticism and contact hitting when it came to their position players, while encouraging situational awareness all through their system. This year's club is the most advanced manifestation of that approach.

On the pitching side, the Brewers are a mix of internally developed hurlers such as Jacob Misiorowski, Robert Gasser and Logan Henderson, along with a number of acquired pitchers. Milwaukee has had an inordinate amount of success in coaxing better results from such pitchers.

Payroll power: Bottom third.

Per Cot's Contracts, the highest the Brewers have ranked in Opening Day payroll during their current 10-year run of success is 17th, back in 2019. They've won four straight National League Central titles while ranking no higher than 20th, where they were in 2026. Milwaukee has an avid and loyal fanbase that keeps attendance numbers strong. But for now, the non-attendance revenue potential of the Brewers is constricted by their market size.

Homegrown percentage: 32%

According to Fangraphs, the Brewers' 40-man roster is 32% homegrown, ranking 20th, while the 26-man roster is at 38%, ranking 15th. The latter measure is the highest of the four remaining teams. The Brewers tend to acquire external players via trades and waiver claims as opposed to free agency.

Signature signing: prospect extensions

Backup catcher Gary Sanchez is the only veteran free agent on the roster. The signings that have been more in step with the Brewers' philosophy have been extensions, especially to some of their most talented prospects. Jackson Chourio, Cooper Pratt and Luis Lara each signed extensions prior to reaching the majors.

Best trade they've made: Christian Yelich from Miami, 2018

The Jan. 25, 2018, trade for Christian Yelich is one of the defining moments for the current era of Brewers baseball. He won NL MVP honors in his first season and finished second in the balloting the season after. Even as injuries have prevented him from maintaining that level of play, Yelich has continued as a face of the franchise. Along with injured pitcher Brandon Woodruff, Yelich has provided continuity and familiarity as the roster, manager and GM have changed over the years. And, not for nothing, the four players the Brewers sent to Miami in the deal are out of all out of the majors and finished with a combined minus-5.9 career bWAR.

Biggest reclamation project success: Jake Bauers, 2026

This area is a specialty of the Brewers, so a typical season would see at least a couple of examples. It's one of the qualities that makes Milwaukee such a difficult team to project. At midseason, the easy answer here would be pitcher Kyle Harrison but because he faltered late in the season, the still-easy answer is first baseman Bauers.

Never able to establish himself while bouncing around the majors, Bauers finally broke out at age 30 and in his third season for the Brewers. Before 2026, Bauers had a career OPS+ of 84 and was below replacement value (minus-1.2 bWAR). This season, Bauers had a 140 OPS+, put up 3.3 bWAR and led the Brewers with 26 home runs.

Historical baggage: Overpacked.

This is an esoteric way to describe the fact that the Brewers are one of five franchises never to win a title. The "mostly" part applies to the city, because Milwaukee did win a World Series in 1957 when the Braves still resided there. The Brewers have won a single pennant, but that came in the American League, so an NL flag still eludes them as well. Lots of boxes could be checked in the weeks to come.

How the Los Angeles Dodgers were built

Roster style: Star power.

As much as the Dodgers flex their economic might, they are also a top-to-bottom showcase for the current suite of best practices in the baseball industry. Yet, there is no denying the star power on the L.A. roster, nor the payroll commitments that have allowed this collection of All-Stars and Hall of Famers to come together.

Think of it like this: According to Baseball Reference, five of the top 25 position players by career OPS+ played for the Dodgers this season. Also, five of the top 20 pitchers by career ERA+. Say what you want about depth, roster management, cutting-edge strategy -- that's a dazzling truckload of superstar ballplayers.

Payroll power: Industry breaking.

Isn't this what the looming lockout is mostly about? The Dodgers top baseball's revenue charts by a good bit, and the depressing thing about that advantage for the other 29 teams is that if the Dodgers wanted to spend even more, they probably could. Depending on where you get your numbers, you can argue that the Dodgers are only above average when it comes to the portion of their operating revenue that's devoted to the payroll. And yeah, there are luxury tax implications for their level of spending under the current CBA, but there is also all that deferred money to players such as Shohei Ohtani, Kyle Tucker and Blake Snell. You can't blame the Dodgers for leaning in to their advantage. And you can't blame anyone who resents it.

Homegrown percentage: 34%

The Dodgers rank 18th in homegrown percentage for their 40-man roster, per Fangraphs, but just five players on their 26-man postseason roster are internally developed prospects. Only the Rays have a lower count among this year's playoff teams. L.A.'s count could rise if it tweaks its roster for the LCS, but the bottom line would remain true.

While L.A. scouting-and-development successes such as Will Smith and Andy Pages play key roles on the roster, the Dodgers' perpetually fecund farm system is used as much for depth and for trades as it is to add to the Dodgers' star count.

Signature signing: Shohei Ohtani, 2024

It's almost counterintuitive, but how could baseball's largest revenue producer produce even more revenue? How could an ongoing 21st dynasty seemingly without end get even better? How could the Dodgers upgrade a high-powered lineup and a deep and talented rotation when the bar for marginal improvement is so high? The answer to all of these questions, and so many more, is to sign Shohei Ohtani. The Dodgers, suffice to say, have not been disappointed.

Best trade they've made: Mookie Betts, 2020

Time flies, doesn't it? Betts has now played in more seasons and games for the Dodgers than he did for the Red Sox, when he was already a champion and a superstar on a Hall of Fame track. Betts has added two more rings and three more top-five MVP finishes to his résumé as a Dodger. He has also made the unprecedented transition from historically great right fielder to a full-time shortstop. Who does that? Well, Betts, who has already risen to 10th on the Dodgers' career bWAR list -- one spot ahead of Roy Campanella.

Biggest reclamation project success: Max Muncy, 2018

A trope about the Dodgers used to be that when they'd acquire some distressed player struggling for another team, they'd "fix" him. It doesn't seem like that's as much of a thing anymore, if only because other teams have become adept at that practice and it has become a bona fide path to finding first-division contributors.

Muncy is not just a throwback to the days when the Dodgers featured several such players -- Muncy, Chris Taylor, Justin Turner, who really fixed himself but we digress. Now Muncy is far removed from being viewed as a mere rags-to-riches story. He's a Dodgers fixture who ranks fifth in franchise history with 238 home runs.

Historical baggage: Traveling light but still some luggage here.

No NL team has won three straight titles, and the Dodgers are bidding to become the first. That can't happen without another pennant, which would be the Dodgers' 28th. A three-peat would really set this era of Dodger dominance apart historically.

How the Tampa Bay Rays were built

Roster style: Ahead of the curve.

Even though the Rays perennially have a top-10 minor league system, it's startling the degree to which the roster was constructed via trades. Thus we come to a chicken-and-egg problem. Do the Rays play the way they play because that's the style demanded of the players they've acquired? Or were those players acquired because they fit the style of play the Rays want to use? The Rays are always at the extreme of some kind of spectrum.

On offense, they are aggressive, make contact and mix a heavy dose of small-ball principles that is accented by the power of Junior Caminero. In run prevention, the Rays have leaned heavily on a staff that uses changeups as a knock-out pitch.

Whatever the Rays are doing, don't try to copy it because by the time you have it implemented, they will be on to the next thing.

Payroll power: Lean and mean.

The Rays invariably land as a bottom-five payroll team. Their focus is on developing and trading for controllable players. The most talented of them are either extended early or traded in advance of an expensive free agency. They are aggressive when it comes to minor league free agents and waiver-wire pickups because of their ability to develop even players with a good amount of big league experience. The roster is always lean financially and is iterated constantly.

Homegrown percentage: 18%

First baseman Jonathan Aranda was an international signing. Left fielder Chandler Simpson and left-handed pitcher Ian Seymour were second-round picks, and shortstop Taylor Walls was taken in the third. That's it. Everyone else on the Rays' division series roster was acquired from another organization or via free agency. The picture doesn't change much from a 40-man roster perspective, yielding the number above from Fangraphs. It's the lowest in baseball.

Signature signing: Nick Martinez

It was only a one-year deal for $9 million, plus a mutual option for 2027, but the Martinez signing last offseason was just such a Rays thing to do. Martinez was a respected pitcher who had some previous big league success, but through his age-34 season, he had 11.1 career bWAR with a 103 ERA+, including a 98 ERA+ for Cincinnati last season. This season for the Rays, he went 15-6 with a 3.10 ERA and a 137 ERA+, threw a career-high 180 innings and posted 3.9 bWAR.

But beyond the late-career leveling up, Martinez also fit the paradigm of what kind of staff the Rays wanted to feature. The Rays threw 750 more changeups than any other team this season. Two of the top 13 individual pitchers were Rays: Freddy Peralta, acquired from the Mets during the season, and Martinez.

Best trade they've made: Junior Caminero

The aging joke is that teams simply should hang up the phone when the Rays call. If they want one of your players, even one you're willing to deal, don't send that player to the Rays because you will lose the trade. Better to figure out what the Rays like in a player and focus on that.

Anyway, of all the trades the Rays have won, acquiring Caminero from Cleveland for Tobias Myers stands out on the current roster because of how good he has become, not to mention how fast. Caminero's 94 career homers rank as the ninth most for a player through his age-22 season. Myers never played in the majors for Cleveland.

Biggest reclamation project success: Yandy Diaz

This is yet another Rays forte, so there are lots to choose from. Diaz hadn't flamed out when he was acquired by the Rays in a three-team 2018 trade from Cleveland. (Guardians: When the Rays call, hang up the phone!) In fact, he hit .312 in his last Cleveland season, albeit over just 39 games. He was, and is, built like an Adonis, but at that point he was through his age-26 season and owned a single big league homer. His narrative was that his power was wasted because he hit the ball on the ground far too often.

One way the Rays excel in secondary development is to focus on what a player does well, not on what he doesn't, and leverage that. He still sports a groundball rate way above the league average. He's also one of the best hitters in baseball. Over eight seasons with the Rays, he has 130 OPS+ and a batting title in 2023. This season he led the American League in hits.

Historical baggage: Nothing to lose.

The Rays have long been identified as the team no one goes to watch that plays in what looks like an upside down plaster basin and that punches above its weight competitively through the guile and cunning of its baseball operations department. It's an amazing narrative and if the narrative changes into something else when the Rays move into their new ballpark, it'll be bittersweet. But despite all of that success and cunning, the Rays have not won a World Series.

How the Cleveland Guardians were built

Roster style: Guardians-specific.

Cleveland's pitching pipeline has been one of the most productive for a number of years and after a slight lag in the rotation department in recent years, the Guardians' have reasserted their ability to develop hurlers.

Like the other two small-market clubs in the final four, Cleveland's offense has a heavy emphasis on making contact and moving runners around the bases, though the Guardians have been considerably less successful than the Rays and Brewers when it comes to turning that approach into consistent runs.

Cleveland's relative lack of power is in part due to a lack of success in getting their best power prospects to go deep consistently in the majors. Angel Martinez led the club with just 18 homers, a big part of why Cleveland targeted ex-Angel Jo Adell and his power bat. One thing that sets the Guardians apart is their adoration of switch-hitters. Cleveland got 2,003 plate appearances from switchers this season, most in the majors.

Payroll power: Dormant.

The Guardians continually cycle through controllable players, keeping the roster young and inexpensive, with Jose Ramirez serving as the notable exception. According to Cot's Contracts, the Guardians' Opening Day payroll was the lowest in baseball and they've generally been bottom five in the current decade despite a lot of on-field success.

This of course is a theme of this year's LCS round. If you subtract the Opening Day payrolls of the Guardians, Rays and Brewers from that of the Dodgers, you'd still have $35.6 million left over, using Cot's numbers.

Homegrown percentage: 58%

According to Fangraphs, the Guardians' 40-man roster is just 1% behind St. Louis for the highest figure in baseball. The 26-man LDS roster featured 16 internally developed players, just three shy of the combined total of the Rays, Brewers and Dodgers. The Guardians scout 'em and develop 'em.

Signature signing: Jose Ramirez

There's nothing close to a splashy free agent signee on the Guardians' roster, but the three extensions Ramirez has signed have been immeasurably important to this franchise. Ramirez's time with the club extends back to its last pennant win in 2016, and his omnipresence in the infield has given the team continuity. He has been an always-there star to a generation of young Cleveland baseball fans. The third of those extensions, signed in January, will keep Ramirez with the club through the 2032 season and all but ensures that he will eventually become a one-team Hall of Famer for the Guardians.

Best trade they've made: Jo Adell

The Guardians aren't heavy traders, another thing that sets them apart from the swap-happy Rays and Brewers. Their relative lack of activity during baseball's heaviest trade periods -- the in-season deadline and the hot stove circuit -- has often been maddening. Cleveland shook things up in 2026, acquiring Adell, Nathaniel Lowe, Patrick Bailey and Foster Griffin during the season.

They have all contributed, but it's Adell's presence in the middle of the power-starved lineup that has most changed the look of the club. Not all players would embrace moving from Los Angeles to Cleveland, but Adell has, and it's easy to envision him having a long, productive relationship with the Guardians.

Biggest reclamation project success: Cade Smith

The Guardians don't really have the same reputation for "fixing" players as do the Rays, Brewers and Dodgers. So we have to get a little creative here and go with Smith, an undrafted free agent pickup in 2020, when the draft was only five rounds long. (He was drafted by the Twins in 2017 but did not sign.) To go from off the draft board to the game's best closer in six years is a nice bit of work by Smith -- and the Guardians.

Historical baggage: a backpack with an anvil in it

It's as simple as this: Cleveland has not won the World Series since 1948, giving it the longest active title drought in the majors. It's a crown it has worn since losing Game 7 to the Cubs in 2016. This season marks the second time the Guardians have gotten this deep in the playoffs since that fateful November night a decade ago. Each year Cleveland falls just short, that anvil gets a little bit heavier.

stories.headline: When can Kimi Antonelli win the F1 title? Earliest date, points needed and remaining races
stories.summary: Kimi Antonelli took another big step towards his first world title after outscoring his two closest championship rivals, George Russell and Lewis Hamilton, at the Singapore Grand Prix.
stories.body:
Kimi Antonelli took another big step towards his first world title after outscoring his two closest championship rivals, George Russell and Lewis Hamilton, at the Singapore Grand Prix.

The 20-year-old, who has the potential to set a new record for the youngest Formula 1 champion this year, now leads Mercedes teammate Russell by 102 points in the standings with a maximum of 150 points still up for grabs.

The substantial lead means he could be crowned champion as early as Oct. 24 at the U.S. Grand Prix in Austin, but the maths around that calculation are slightly complicated by question marks over the final two races of the season. The grands prix in Qatar and Abu Dhabi are currently scheduled to go ahead on Nov. 29 and Dec. 6, but escalations in the war between the United States and Iran have the potential to force the cancellation of both rounds.

F1 has put a contingency plan in place to hold a single round at Imola if Qatar and Abu Dhabi are cancelled, but doing so would cut the championship short by one round and mean only 125 points are available to any single driver before the end of the year. Such a scenario would change the maths around the championship fight, making it easier for Antonelli to be crowned champion in Austin.

- 'Chucky' Verstappen is back. Luckily for Antonelli and Mercedes, it's too late

- Max Verstappen takes back-to-back wins with dominant drive at Singapore GP

- Lewis Hamilton calls Singapore GP strategy 'painful lesson' after Ferrari apology

Alongside Russell and Hamilton, Max Verstappen, Charles Leclerc and Lando Norris are still mathematically in contention for this year's championship, although the incredibly slim hopes of Leclerc and Norris would be snuffed out entirely by the cancellation of the races in the Middle East.

What does Antonelli need to do to be crowned champion in Austin?
Assuming the final two races go ahead as planned, Antonelli's chances of clinching the title in Austin remain relatively slim. The Mercedes driver would need to win in Texas, with his teammate Russell finishing ninth or lower and Hamilton finishing fifth or lower.

Such a scenario would put Antonelli 125 points ahead of Russell with 125 points remaining, but even if Antonelli failed to score another point and Russell won all the remaining rounds after Austin, Antonelli would still be crowned champion on countback of race victories (by that stage Antonelli would be on nine and Russell on three with five races remaining).

If the championship is shortened by the season ending in Imola rather than Abu Dhabi, Antonelli would only need to leave Austin with a lead of 100 points over his rivals.

Such a scenario would result in the following permutations:

If Antonelli wins in Austin he would be crowned champion regardless of where the others finish.
If Antonelli finishes second, he would be crowned champion if Russell doesn't win the race.
If Antonelli finishes third, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes off the podium.
If Antonelli finishes fourth, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes behind him and Hamilton does not win the race.
If Antonelli finishes fifth, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes fourth or lower and Hamilton does not win the race.
If Antonelli finishes sixth, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes fifth or lower and Hamilton does not win the race.
If Antonelli finishes seventh, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes sixth or lower and Hamilton does not finish in the top two.
If Antonelli finishes eighth, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes seventh or lower, Hamilton does not finish in the top two and Verstappen does not win the race.
If Antonelli finishes ninth, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes eighth or lower, Hamilton does not finish in the top three and Verstappen does not win the race.
If Antonelli finishes tenth, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes ninth or lower, Hamilton does not finish in the top three and Verstappen does not win the race.
If Antonelli fails to score, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes ninth or lower, Hamilton finishes fifth or lower and Verstappen does not win the race.

What's the minimum Antonelli needs to do be crowned champion?
Another way to look at the championship is the minimum amount of points Antonelli needs to score over the remaining rounds to secure the title regardless of what other drivers achieve. Assuming Qatar and Abu Dhabi go ahead, he needs 49 points over the remaining rounds, which could be achieved with as little as five sixth place finishes and one fifth place finish over the rest of the season.

If only five races remain, Antonelli would need just 24 points to secure the title, which would be attainable with two seventh place finishes and three eighth place finishes at the remaining rounds.

stories.headline: 'Disjointed' WNBA causing WNBL scheduling issues
stories.summary: One of the WNBL's star players has labelled an overlap between the WNBA and Australia's domestic season "hard" ahead of the league's tip-off on Thursday.
stories.body:
The WNBL is considering pushing back the start of next season's competition, with several big-name players expected to miss the opening games of the upcoming campaign.

Reigning league MVP Isobel Borlase (Bendigo), Opal Miela Sowah (Townsville) and import Madina Okot (Tasmania) will not feature in at least the opening two weekends of the Australian competition when it begins on Thursday.

They will instead be competing in the WNBA finals, where Borlase and Okot are looking to deliver the Atlanta Dream their first title, while Sowah is part of the Golden State Valkyries' fairytale run.

With the FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup held in September, the American competition stopped for 17 days and subsequently ended later than scheduled.

This means the league has directly clashed with the start of the WNBL campaign.

Making matters worse, in 2027 the WNBA is expanding the number of regular-season games, meaning the competition will run until November.

With the prospect of WNBL imports and Australian Opals still playing overseas, there is a huge risk that marquee players could miss the opening month of the league if it starts in October, as it does this season.

"We're always considering what the best possible situation is for not only Australians but other international players that want to play in the WNBL," the league's chief operating officer Justin Nelson told AAP.

"Is there the prospect of maybe starting a little bit later? The short answer is yes.

"But how much we may or may not move is still to be seen."

Adelaide Lightning coach Aja Parham-Ammar is waiting to see how Opal Steph Talbot pulls up after her Las Vegas Aces were knocked out of the WNBA semi-finals on Saturday (AEDT).

The Lightning play the Sydney Flames on Sunday, but of bigger concern beyond whether she will play is that Talbot has missed all of the team's pre-season.

"It (not having Talbot) can be disruptive or disjointed a bit, but you've got to be grateful that you have talent that's playing at the highest level," the coach told AAP.

"It (moving the season back) is definitely a conversation to be had. With WNBA being the top league, you want to be able to bring that top talent over and not create issues with recruiting."

Also in a sticky situation are the Geelong Venom, who have recruited towering superstar Han Xu.

The Chinese national was part of the New York Liberty side that lost the semi-final against Atlanta, and it is unclear if she will feature in the WNBL season opener against the Tasmania Jewels on Thursday.

Regardless, star guard Bec Cole says the Venom will back themselves to win.

"We can still beat teams without Han, and then (when Geelong) bring her in there'll be an adjustment period because she's going to be a big facet of what we do," Cole told AAP.

"It is hard, and we are a new team, but that's just the game of basketball, and we're all professional."

stories.headline: Ranking every AFL free agent by the impact they'll have at their new club
stories.summary: The 2026 AFL free agency period is now complete. We've ranked every move that has been made, factoring in positional needs and their likely impact for season 2027.
stories.body:
The 2026 AFL free agency period is now complete, with seven players finding new clubs either as restricted or unrestricted free agents.

We've ranked every move that has been made, factoring in positional needs and their likely impact for season 2027 (not the rest of their career). So, who will be the biggest needle mover of the bunch in the immediate future?

7. Kieren Briggs
This is absolutely no criticism of Kieren Briggs, but there really aren't many players in the competition (if any) that could be dropped into the Tigers in 2027 and be serious needle movers. Remember, Richmond has won just 10 games across the last three seasons and is widely expected to finish in the bottom four once again next year. Tigers skipper Toby Nankervis will remain the club's primary ruck in the immediate future, but the arrival of Briggs will allow for a new-look one-two punch. The former Giant is one of the best hitout-to-advantage rucks in the game and an elite clearance winner. At 27 years of age, and with Nankervis now 32, Briggs' impact will likely be felt in the years beyond 2027.

6. Jordon Butts
Key defensive stocks have been a concern for the Bulldogs in recent years, so the signing of Jordon Butts will be a welcomed addition for the club. Butts makes the move after eight seasons and 94 games with the Crows, but he's managed just 10 and nine games in 2025 and 2026. Throughout different parts of the last couple of years, he's struggled with unlucky injuries; in 2025 it was a collapsed lung, and this year he battled concussion and a fractured foot. With the continued strong form of Josh Worrell and Mark Keane, and emergence of Josh Borlase at the Crows, a move to the Bulldogs makes sense for both the 26-year-old Butts and the Dogs.

5. Joel Amartey
The Blues landed key forward support for Harry McKay in the form of Joel Amartey, who crosses from the Swans as an unrestricted free agent. It's a shrewd acquisition for Carlton, and the club will be hopeful he can be an upgrade on both Brodie Kemp and Mitch McGovern. Amartey is coming off a season at Sydney in which he booted 28 goals from 15 games and averaged three marks per game. In 2024 he enjoyed a career-best 43-goal campaign, including a bag of nine against the Crows. Amartey is just 27 years of age and should only really be coming into his prime as a key position player in the AFL. Could surprise a few in 2027.

4. Toby Greene
Another year, another major coup for the Cats. Is anyone surprised?! Former Giants captain Toby Greene joins Geelong as an unrestricted free agent while GWS has to make do with second-round compensation. We all know Greene has been a high-impact player throughout his 15-year career and he will add a whole new dynamic to the Cats' forward line, one that features former Giants teammate and close friend Jeremy Cameron. In 2026, Greene kicked 34 goals -- his lowest return in a season since his injury-interrupted 2020 campaign -- but did amass over 20 disposals per game. If anyone wanted to argue he deserves the top spot on this list I wouldn't scoff, but it's not as if the Cats had trouble scoring in 2026...

3. Ben King
It may have been a move that surprised few, but it's one -- along with the signing of Zach Merrett, of course -- that will have Hawks fans believing a premiership is possible in 2027. For a fair chunk of the 2026 season, King looked to be the Coleman Medal winner. Gold Coast's capitulation didn't help his chances, though he still finished the home and away season with 60 goals to his name -- the third consecutive year he's managed 55+ goals. King will partner veteran Jack Gunston and dynamo Nick Watson in what now looks to be one of the most dangerous forward lines in the game.

2. Lachie Neale
The Lachie Neale-Brisbane Lions era is over, with the two-time Brownlow Medal winner joining Collingwood as an unrestricted free agent and partnering reigning Brownlow winner Nick Daicos in a new-look Magpies midfield. Neale might be 33 years of age and on the downturn of his decorated career, but he still averaged 29 disposals, 12.5 contested possessions, and six clearances per outing in 2026 and figures to be a major contributor next season in a Collingwood engine room that's often lacked depth and firepower. Even if the Magpies receive 80-85% of this season's production from Neale, he'll be difficult to top as the most impactful free agent of the year.

1. Zak Butters
The most sought after man in football made the decision to sign with the Bulldogs during free agency. Former Power star Zak Butters joins the club as a top five player in the game, and at age 26, you can certainly make the argument he's only at the beginning of his prime. Butters will partner Western Bulldogs skipper Marcus Bontempelli and Ed Richards in what's easily the most impressive and dynamic three-pronged midfield in the competition. He offers a real point of difference, too, with his electric pace and the ability to break lines two eye-catching features that have seen him ascend to footy superstardom.

stories.headline: Denkey's double sparks Cincinnati to win over Atlanta
stories.summary: Kevin Denkey scored two goals after a scoreless first half and FC Cincinnati snapped a six-match winless streak with a 3-1 victory over Atlanta United on Saturday night.
stories.body:
ATLANTA -- Kevin Denkey scored two goals after a scoreless first half and FC Cincinnati snapped a six-match winless streak with a 3-1 victory over Atlanta United on Saturday night.

Denkey scored in the 52nd minute to give Cincinnati (9-9-9) a 1-0 lead. Tom Barlow and David Douděra had assists.

Miguel Almirón used passes from Breel Embolo and Tomás Jacob to score his fifth goal and tie it 1-all in the 69th minute.

Kyle Smith set up Tom Barlow for the go-ahead goal in the 84th minute, and Denkey scored in the seventh minute of stoppage time to wrap up the victory.

Denkey has 16 goals on the season, one more than he had last year in his first 29 league appearances.

Barlow has eight goals and four assists this season - both career highs through 200 career matches.

Evan Louro turned away five shots in his third start in goal this season for Cincinnati and the eighth of his career.

Lucas Hoyos had one save for Atlanta United (7-15-6) in his first MLS campaign.

Cincinnati improves to 2-7-6 on the road while ending an 0-3-3 stretch overall. The club beat Atlanta United 2-0 at home in the season opener to complete the sweep.

Atlanta United saw a three-match unbeaten run end while falling to 4-8-2 at home.

Up next Cincinnati: Hosts New England Revolution on Wednesday.

Atlanta: At CF Montreal on Wednesday.

stories.headline: New Zealand Rugby launches legal action against ARLC over 'Chiefs' name
stories.summary: The battle over the use of the "Chiefs" name is headed to the New Zealand High Court after New Zealand Rugby launched legal action against the Australian Rugby League Commission.
stories.body:
The battle over the use of the "Chiefs" name is headed to the New Zealand High Court after New Zealand Rugby launched legal action against the Australian Rugby League Commission.

NZR on Thursday said it had been left with no choice but to launch legal proceedings against the ARLC, who has sought to adopt the name for its Papua New Guinea expansion franchise.

The PNG Chiefs are due to join the NRL in 2028 and have already signed a raft of players, including code-hoppers Zac Lomaz and Joey Manu, but they may yet have to undergo a chanGe of name if NZR gets its way.

The Chiefs' Super Rugby franchise has existed since 1996, with NZR claiming the introduction of the PNG Chiefs would result in "significant confusion and damage" should they be allowed to compete under the name from 2028.

"New Zealand Rugby (NZR) has today moved to protect the Chiefs brand and is filing proceedings in the High Court of New Zealand against the decision by the Australian Rugby League Commission (ARLC) to launch a new NRL side using "Chiefs" in its name," an NZR statement read.  

"NZR is seeking both an interim and final injunction which stops the use of the names 'PNG Chiefs', 'Chiefs' or any other similar names in New Zealand.   

"The Chiefs have competed as a professional rugby team in Super Rugby since 1996 and over those 30 years, have built a strong identity and fanbase across New Zealand, Australia and internationally.  

"In New Zealand, NZR owns both the trademark rights for the word Chiefs and the Chiefs logo and since 1998, NZR has also held trademark protection for the Chiefs logo in Australia."

NZR claims it had tried to engage with the ARLC in an attempt to find a resolution, yet the commission was now intent on proceeding with the official launch of the PNG Chiefs on Oct. 21.

"For 30 years the Chiefs and their players have built an incredibly strong identity that is widely recognised and loved by fans," NZR chief executive Steve Lancaster said. "We have raised our concerns with the ARLC directly and consistently over the last year in attempting to find a resolution. We now have a responsibility to protect the Chiefs brand.   

"We want to be absolutely clear, this is not about rugby league's growth in the Pacific. We welcome the development of the Pacific region through sport and the passion that the people of Papua New Guinea have for both rugby and rugby league."  

The Chiefs won two Super Rugby titles in back-to-back seasons in 2012 and 2013, and were runners-up in Super Rugby Pacific this season after suffering a crushing defeat by the Hurricanes in the decider.

The Hamilton-based team has produced countless All Blacks since its inception, with Saturday's run-on team to face the Wallabies featuring six players from the franchise.

"Here in New Zealand, when people hear 'the Chiefs', they think of this club and this region. The identity carries significant cultural meaning and connection to the region and its people, we know it means a great deal to our players and coaches past and present, fans and supporters here and around the world," Chiefs CEO Simon Graafhuis said.   

"Teams in different sports and markets can exist alongside one another with the same name, but the issue here is the similarity of our sports competing in the same market, for the same fans, in overlapping windows."  

However, ARLC executive chairman Peter V'Landys later issued a stinging rebuke, insisting he would vigorously defend PNG's right to use the Chiefs as its team name.

"The hypocrisy is mind-blowing, considering the Auckland Blues in 1996 used the NSW Blues name without any consultation or approval. The NSW Blues had been the Blues for in excess of 50 years before that," he said.

"Rugby union is obviously feeling threatened by rugby league in New Zealand, with sell-outs at most rugby league games."

No date has yet been slated for the hearing in New Zealand's High Court.
